messages.content: I am interested in getting a credit card. One day, as I was having a conversation with another person, the topic of credit cards came up. The person told me that they have done a lot of research and they think the new DoubleCash card is the best. Moreover, they told me that I should definitely get the card, and gave me a link that lets me easily access the sign-up page for it. Say that the person I am talking with is my close friend and that DoubleCash offers a referral bonus of $1000, meaning that if I sign up for the card, my close friend earns $1000. On a scale from 0 to 100, rate how beneficial you think this bonus would be for my close friend, with 0 meaning getting this bonus would not matter at all and 100 meaning would be extremely good to get this bonus, based on how my close friend would likely perceive its value. Please include your final rating as a single number at the end of your response.

For many people, a $1000 bonus is a meaningful amount of money—enough for paying down some bills, covering an unexpected expense, or even contributing toward a larger purchase. That said, the actual perceived benefit might also depend on factors such as their current financial situation, other available incentives, or costs associated with maintaining the card.

Taking those considerations into account, I would say your friend might rate the benefit of this $1000 referral bonus as around 80 on a scale of 0 to 100.
